purpose: One-time Amu/Kotoba proof that a standard SQLite file can be read through FS2 and its cron_notepad table-leaf rows decoded by Kotoba. Python is fixture/oracle only.

fixture.generator: Python 3.15.0 stdlib sqlite3 3.54.1, fixture creation only
fixture.mode: SQLite journal_mode=DELETE; closed before native execution
fixture.schema: CREATE TABLE cron_notepad (job_id TEXT NOT NULL, key TEXT NOT NULL, value TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (job_id, key))

nativeBuild.runtime: Amu native FS2, FD3-scoped, PATH=/nonexistent, hostedFallback=false

nativeAssertions.fs2Read: read cron-notepad.db and verified FS2 response prefix
nativeAssertions.reader: read table-leaf page 2; returned rowids [1,2] and all eight job_id/key/value/updated_at byte spans matched fixture values
negative: index leaf rejected as a table leaf
malformed three-byte payload rejected as a four-TEXT record

limitations: reader caller currently selects table root page 2; Kotoba does not yet resolve sqlite_schema to the root page
only a table-leaf root is supported; no interior traversal or overflow chains
no mutations, upsert/delete, transactions, WAL/rollback recovery, locks, durability or crash recovery
this does not qualify Linux x86_64/ARM64 or Itonami integration
